what: p measured PER TEMPERATURE RUNG on the Radeon, and the corrected prediction
why_it_matters: 1-(1-p)^K assumes one p for all K draws. VerifiedSearch draws across a temperature ladder, so the correct form is 1 - PROD(1 - p_rung). Where the two disagree, the equation was not wrong -- it was being applied to draws it does not describe.

effective_k_analysis.conclusion: 1-(1-p)^K is not wrong; it was applied with the wrong K. On a task this model finds hard, every draw at t<=0.6 has p=0.00 -- so a NOMINAL K of 8 is an EFFECTIVE K of 4. With p on the productive rungs anywhere in 0.05-0.10 (1/10 is a coarse estimate) the prediction is 0.185-0.344 against 0.167 observed, which is consistent. The diversity ladder buys coverage on easy tasks and spends half the batch on nothing when the task is hard.
effective_k_analysis.greedy_rung_is_deterministic: t=0.0 produced 1 distinct completion in 10 draws, measured here on the GPU. That is the same degeneracy that made an earlier harness report 112/112 p=1.000 by calling build_from_idea(k=1) sixteen times -- sixteen draws at temperature 0 are one draw. Independently confirmed on real hardware rather than argued from the source.
